overall: Temperatures have been remarkably flat all morning, sitting at 63-64°F from 3am through 10:52 ET before ticking up to 64.9°F by 11:16 ET. The near-saturated dewpoint of 63.0°F (essentially at parity with air temp) and persistent NE onshore flow of ~8 mph are suppressing daytime heating, and the day is tracking well below the NWS headline high of 72°F. Skies are mostly cloudy with a 40% rain chance further limiting solar insolation.
forecast_obs_notes: NWP models show unusually wide disagreement, ranging from GFS at 67.8°F to ECMWF at 73.6°F — a nearly 6°F spread — with HRRR (69.5°F) and NBM (72.7°F) in between. Observed temperatures are running closest to the GFS solution and well below ECMWF/NBM, suggesting the cooler end of the model envelope is more credible given the moisture-laden boundary layer and marine-influenced flow keeping a lid on warming.
max_temp_prediction: With a current running max of 64.9°F at 11:16 ET and a predicted peak around 14:12 ET (roughly 3 hours away), even at the observed +1.4°F/hr velocity (which is decelerating per the trend slope of -0.032°F/hr²), gains will be limited by the high dewpoint and clouds. The META model — the most reliable signal — puts 44.6% probability on the 68-69°F bucket, with secondary weight on 66-67°F (23.8%) and 70-71°F (16.3%). The active odd-bucket market's top bucket of 69-70°F at 20.9% is consistent but the META favors landing just under 69°F. Confidence is moderate; ensemble signals recommend no trade given model spread and uncertainty.
